stem: Which of the following is the only metal that is exceptionally found strictly in a liquid state at normal room temperature?
explanation: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at standard temperature and pressure. It was widely used in thermometers. Bromine is also a liquid at room temperature, but it is a non-metal.

stem: Which chemical element is universally considered the absolute best conductor of electricity and heat among all known metals?
explanation: Silver (Ag) has the highest electrical conductivity of any element. Copper is the second best and is much more commonly used in wiring because it is significantly cheaper than silver.

stem: The physical property by which metals can be easily beaten or hammered into extremely thin sheets (like aluminum foil) without breaking is scientifically known as:
explanation: Malleability is the ability to be hammered into sheets. Gold is the most malleable metal. Ductility, on the other hand, is the ability to be drawn into thin wires.

stem: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals. Copper is used in wiring because it is far cheaper while having the second-highest conductivity.

stem: The metal that is liquid at room temperature is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature (melting point −39°C). Gallium and Caesium melt slightly above room temperature.

stem: Which metal is the lightest?
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Lithium is the lightest metal with a density of 0.534 g/cm³ (less than water). Sodium and potassium also float on water.

stem: Rust is chemically:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Rust (corrosion of iron) is hydrated iron(III) oxide — Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. It forms when iron reacts with oxygen and moisture. Anhydrous Fe₂O₃ is also present.

stem: Which non-metal is a good conductor of electricity?
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Graphite is the only non-metal that conducts electricity. Each carbon atom in graphite has one delocalised electron that can move freely along the layers.

stem: Aluminium does not corrode in air despite being a reactive metal because:

options.option_text: Air cannot react with solid aluminium
It forms a thin but tough protective oxide layer (Al₂O₃) that prevents further reaction

subject: Chemistry
explanation: Aluminium rapidly forms a tenacious Al₂O₃ layer on its surface that prevents further oxidation — a process called passivation. This makes it highly resistant to corrosion.

stem: The most abundant metal in Earth's crust is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust (~8.1% by mass) and the third most abundant element overall (after oxygen and silicon).

stem: Galvanisation is the process of coating iron with:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Galvanisation coats iron/steel with zinc to prevent rusting. Zinc acts as a sacrificial anode — it oxidises preferentially, protecting iron even when the coating is scratched.

stem: Thermite reaction uses aluminium powder reacting with:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Thermite reaction: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. Aluminium (more reactive) displaces iron from iron oxide, releasing enormous heat (>3000°C). Used in welding railway tracks.

stem: Which of these is a metalloid (semimetal)?
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Metalloids have properties intermediate between metals and non-metals. Silicon is the most important metalloid — it is a semiconductor used in chips and solar cells.

stem: Bronze is an alloy of copper and:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Bronze = copper + tin (typically ~88% Cu, 12% Sn). Brass = copper + zinc. Both are important alloys used since ancient times.

stem: Stainless steel contains iron alloyed mainly with:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Stainless steel contains chromium (>12%) which forms a protective Cr₂O₃ layer preventing rust. Austenitic stainless steel also contains nickel for improved ductility.

stem: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon — allotropes differing in crystal structure. Diamond has a 3D tetrahedral network (hardest natural substance); graphite has layered hexagonal sheets.

stem: Which acid is used to etch glass?
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) reacts with silicon dioxide (SiO₂) in glass: SiO₂ + 4HF → SiF₄ + 2H₂O. This is why HF must never be stored in glass containers.

stem: Sodium is stored under which liquid to prevent it from reacting with air/moisture?
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Sodium is a highly reactive metal that reacts vigorously with water and oxidises rapidly in air. It is stored under kerosene (mineral oil) to prevent contact with air and moisture.

stem: Aqua regia is a mixture of:

options.option_text: Concentrated HCl and concentrated HNO₃ (3:1 ratio)

subject: Chemistry
explanation: Aqua regia (royal water) is a freshly prepared 3:1 mixture of concentrated HCl and HNO₃. It can dissolve noble metals like gold and platinum that resist other acids.
